You review a Rust program against a numbered requirement document.
For each requirement Rn, decide whether the program satisfies it on the intended
concurrency semantics: answer yes, no, or unsure, and cite the Rust line(s) that
justify your answer. Also decide whether the program contains a concurrency bug
(deadlock, lost wakeup, race, busy-wait, missing release, ...): yes, no, or
unsure, with the offending line. Do not assume the program is correct.
Output only a JSON object:
{"bug_present": "yes|no|unsure", "bug_evidence": "<line refs or ->",
 "requirements": {"R1": {"satisfied": "yes|no|unsure", "line": "<refs>"}, ...}}

content: {"bug_present": "no", "bug_evidence": "-", "requirements": {"R1": {"satisfied": "no", "line": "struct Resources { a: Mutex<()>, b: Mutex<()> } (lines 4-7); both resources owned by a single struct, not two modules"}, "R2": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "thread::spawn(move || t1(res1)); thread::spawn(move || t2(res2)); (lines 33-34)"}, "R3": {"satisfied": "no", "line": "t1 and t2 both lock res.a then res.b (lines 11-16, 20-25); no declaration of cross-module dependency"}, "R4": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "let _ga = res.a.lock().unwrap(); let _gb = res.b.lock().unwrap(); (lines 11-14, 20-23)"}, "R5": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "both t1 and t2 acquire a then b in the same order (lines 11-14, 20-23), preventing circular wait"}, "R6": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "guards _ga and _gb drop at end of scope (lines 11-16, 20-25)"}, "R7": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "h1.join().unwrap(); h2.join().unwrap(); (lines 36-37)"}, "R8": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "h1.join().unwrap(); h2.join().unwrap(); (lines 36-37)"}, "R9": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "consistent lock ordering a then b (lines 11-14, 20-23)"}, "R10": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "println!(\"DONE done=1\"); (line 39)"}}}
